identity.title: Powered Industrial Truck Pre-Shift Inspection Log

scan.summary: This is an inspection log for a propane-powered forklift (Toyota 8FGU25, unit FL-2) at the Portland warehouse for September 2026. The log records pre-shift inspections of 12 safety-critical items per OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7), with entries on 11 dates showing mostly passes (checkmarks) and one defect (horn failure on Sep 9). The document provides evidence that required inspections are being performed and recorded.
scan.freshness_note: This log covers September 1–18, 2026. The most recent entry is Sep 18, which is 9 days old as of today (Sep 27, 2026). The log is current but incomplete—it appears to be a month-to-date record still in use.

gaps.title: Missing inspections for Sep 3–6
gaps.description: The log shows no inspection entries for September 3, 4, 5, or 6, 2026. The document itself notes that 'the hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days,' confirming the truck was in use but no inspection record exists.
gaps.fix: Conduct and record pre-shift inspections for all shifts on which the truck operates. If the truck did not run on those dates, clarify the schedule. If inspections were performed but not recorded, backfill the log with dates, times, and operator names.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'Before being put into use and at least daily, powered industrial trucks shall be examined by the person designated to operate the truck to ensure that the truck is in safe operating condition.'
gaps.locator: between Sep 2 and Sep 7 entries, page 1
gaps.quote: The hour meter rises between Sep 2 (4,819) and Sep 7 (4,834), which shows the truck ran on the missing days.

gaps.title: Defect not resolved
gaps.description: On Sep 9, a horn defect was recorded ('Horn not working'). The log shows the horn passed inspection on Sep 10 and all subsequent dates, but there is no documentation of when the horn was repaired, by whom, or what action was taken between Sep 9 and Sep 10 to correct the defect.
gaps.fix: Add a note in the log explaining the repair action taken (e.g., 'Horn repaired Sep 9, 15:30 by [technician name]'). If the truck continued in use despite the defect on Sep 9, document the reason and any compensating controls. OSHA requires that trucks with defects affecting safety not be used.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7): 'do not use if a defect affects safety'

gaps.title: Supervisor review not signed
gaps.description: The log template includes a line for 'Supervisor review: ____________________ Date: __________' on page 2, but both fields are blank. The log does not show evidence of supervisory oversight or verification of the inspection records.
gaps.fix: Have a supervisor review and sign the log at the end of each shift, week, or month (depending on company procedure) with the date, to confirm that inspections were performed correctly and defects were addressed.
gaps.citation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.178(q)(7) does not explicitly require a supervisor signature, but OSHA expects records to be reviewed. Oregon administrative rules or company safety procedures may require it; verify local requirements.
